doc: Labelled accuracy set for the backlink spam label (G18). Every row is a REAL referring site with the fields the ledger sees, taken from the runs named in `source`; `label` is the judgement a careful human gives after looking at the referring page. The scorer (score.js) feeds the rows through the real *Parse Backlinks* node (the D3 footprint gate inside it) and scores its `link_type === 'spam'` against the labels. Precision must stay at or above 95% (scenario S49). Nothing here is fetched or invented: the 16 link-farm rows and the three techand.ai referrers are execution 418 of 2026-10-12 (`files/phase1-live-2026-10-12/backlinks-parse-2026-10-12.json`), the PBN anchor and page title are DataForSEO's own (`harness/fixtures_live/bl_new.json`, real response of 2026-10-02), robuta.com is `bl_lost.json` of the same capture, and the competitor's referrers are execution 418's link gap plus the two real pages kept in `harness/fixtures_live/`. A case may also carry `low_value: true`: the link is genuine but worth nothing for SEO (a search-results page, a scraper's listing), so it must never appear among the site's "best links". score.js reports that as `best_link_precision` — measured and printed, not gated.

targets.note: the site under audit: its own ledger of 2026-10-12 (19 rows) plus robuta.com, a referrer DataForSEO reported on 2026-10-02

a competitor, so that genuine referring sites of a real e-invoicing vendor are scored too: the pages and domains that really link to it (execution 418's link gap, which is DataForSEO's referring-domain data for cleartax.com / azentio.com)
